life_summary: George Albert Smith was born June 26, 1817, in Potsdam, New York, the first cousin of Joseph Smith Jr. He joined the Church at age fifteen in 1832 and later moved to Ohio to meet his famous cousin for the first time. Smith grew to manhood as the religious movement expanded and faced persecution. He married eight women in his lifetime and fathered twenty children, establishing a large and influential family. Known for his distinctive personality, Smith earned a Paiute nickname meaning "takes himself apart" due to his habit of removing his wig and false teeth while preaching to audiences. He was known for his physical appearance and remarkable speaking style.
church_summary: George A. Smith became an ordained apostle in 1839 at age twenty-one. Following Joseph Smith's death, he pioneered westward with Brigham Young's 1847 expedition and helped establish Iron County, Utah, serving as its chief justice. From 1868 until his death in 1875, he served as First Counselor in the First Presidency to President Young. In August 1857, Smith toured southern Utah communities shortly before the Mountain Meadows Massacre; historical accounts suggest his tour, speeches, and personal actions contributed to fear and tension in these communities, though his exact role remains debated by scholars. He dedicated his life to establishing Mormon communities throughout southern Utah.
